value.rationale: The first nonisomorphic equal-edge trees are a natural exact finite contact-process benchmark. A rigorous all-rate mean-survival ranking can oppose finite-deadline probability rankings, with a nontrivial dependence on initial infected count; these precise short-time signs matter for interpreting extinction risk rather than merely repeating a known mean formula. Substantive time-domain structure remains after crediting earlier full-occupancy means.
residual_risks: Does not support extrapolation to larger graphs or stochastic intervention policy without further work.

final_claim: For four-vertex star and path with unit SIS recovery and common infection lambda>0, mean extinction from a uniform k-infected set is greater on the star for k=1,2,3,4; short-time star-minus-path survival sign is (-,+,-,-) at first order t^(k+2), forcing a later crossing for k=1,3,4.
limitations: Same generator as four-patch occupancy dynamics; the earlier all-infected mean polynomial must be attributed.
For k=2 no survival crossing or stochastic domination is claimed.
Positive mean difference forces a later positive signed survival gap but not crossing uniqueness.
